transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I guess... people say my talking gets all mixed up. I try to explain things to them. Like about the keys... and then the jail... the prayer rug, or... the chess pieces. I don't know. They just tell me they can't follow what I'm saying. That's why I'm here.
Have you had any periods when you felt unusually energized or needed much less sleep than usual?

I suppose... yeah. Sometimes I don't need much. Maybe two or three hours. 

I get up before dawn, and... I feel fresh. I just start planning my work for the day. It just feels like sleep is... well, something other people need. Not me.
Have you ever felt unusually excited or irritable for several days in a row?

Yeah... sometimes. I get... I don't know, feeling real high up. Powerful. I'll be laughing, talking loud with everybody at work. 

But... if someone questions me when I'm like that... I can snap. I might shout at them over some little thing. That's about it.
Have you ever had times when you heard or saw things that other people did not, even when your mood was not very high or low?

Yeah. I guess so. 

Even when I'm... not feeling all that high, or... or low. Just normal, I guess. There was a time, maybe a couple weeks or more... I still heard him. The man in the vents. And... I knew the people in the building were still doing it. Signaling to each other about me. 

But... yeah. That happens.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least two weeks when you were having hallucinations or delusional beliefs but your mood was not unusually high or low?

I... I think I just said that. Yeah. 

There were calmer weeks. I wasn't all high up, and I wasn't down in a hole either. Just... regular. But yeah, for more than two weeks... I still heard him. The man in the vents. And I still knew the people in the building were signaling about me. 

It just... it kept happening anyway.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so high or irritable that you needed much less sleep and felt much more energetic or active than usual?

Yeah... I guess so. 

Sometimes I just... don't need it. Sleep, I mean. I'll get maybe two, three hours. Wake up before the sun's even up. But I don't feel tired. I feel... fresh. Ready to go. 

I'll just start planning out my whole shift... like sleep is just... something other people need. Not me. So yeah... that happens for a week or more sometimes.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day?

Yeah. I get those days. 

Sometimes it's... more than two weeks, I guess. I just... I sit on the edge of the bed after morning prayer. And I just feel... heavy. Empty. 

Like there's just no point. No point in cleaning myself up, or... or even going outside. It just... it gets really bad sometimes.
Have there been times when you were hearing or believing these things even while your mood was completely normal for several weeks?

I... didn't you just ask me that? 

I told you... yes. Even when I wasn't feeling so high up... or down in the dirt. Just... regular. For a few weeks. 

I still heard him. In the vents. And I knew they were signaling each other about me. It didn't stop just because my mood was... fine.
Have you ever had a stretch of at least six months when these kinds of symptoms were present?

Yeah... longer than six months. 

It's been... I don't know, maybe two and a half years now? Since... since that time they held me. Over that... misunderstanding at the building I was cleaning. It's been going on since then.
Have you ever had any period when the hallucinations or beliefs went away completely, even though your mood symptoms were still happening?

No. They don't go away. 

Even when I'm... feeling okay, or when I'm down. The voices... and the knowing that they're watching me. It's just... always there. It's been like that for... about a year and a half now. They don't stop.
Have there been any times when you were hearing voices or feeling watched while you were not having any depression or high mood symptoms at all?

You just... you keep asking me this. I already told you. 

Yes. There were calmer weeks. I wasn't... high, and I wasn't deeply depressed. But for more than two weeks, I still heard the man in the vents. I still knew the people in the building were signaling about me. 

I don't know how else to explain it.
Was there ever a period of at least two weeks when you had the voices or felt watched, but you were not having any depression, mania, or high mood symptoms at all?

I just... I just said that. Like I told you a minute ago. 

Yes. There were calm weeks. I wasn't up, and I wasn't down. But for over two weeks... I still heard the guy in the vents. I still knew about the signaling. 

I don't... I don't have a different answer for you.

Have your hallucinations or beliefs about people watching you ever continue for at least two weeks while you were not having any mood symptoms at all, and did that happen for most of the time you’ve been ill?

Yeah. I already said that. The vents... the signaling. That happens even when I'm just... regular.

But... mostly, since this whole thing started... I guess I've been in those... keyed-up times. Where I just talk and talk. And I start these big cleaning jobs that I can't even finish. Just... driven. Like I can't stop. That's... that's been most of it.
When you have the voices or feel watched, are you also feeling unusually high or depressed at the same time?

Yeah... sometimes. When I get like I was saying, where I don't sleep much and I'm making all those big plans for the buildings... the voice in the vents is still there. And the hallway lights, they... I know they're flashing warnings about me at the same time.
Have you ever had a period of at least one week when your mood was so elevated or irritable that you were much more active or energetic than usual?

Yeah... I guess. Sometimes. 

I just... I get to feeling real good. Like... powerful, I guess. I'll be talking loud, laughing with everybody around the building. 

But... if somebody questions me... I don't know. I can snap. Start shouting over some little thing. That's... yeah, that happens.
Have you ever had a time when you felt so energized or wired that you needed very little sleep for at least a week?

Yeah... sometimes. I don't know, I just... I can sleep two or three hours, maybe. Get up way before dawn. 

I feel fine when I do. Fresh, even. I just start planning out the work for the building. It's like... I don't know. Like sleep is just something other people need. Not me.
Have you ever had a time when your depression and the voices or beliefs that people were watching you were happening at the same time?

No... I don't think so. When I get down like that, I just... I don't want to be around anybody. I just stay in my room. I don't really pay attention to the voices or the lights then. I just... want to be left alone.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually inflated or grandiose, like you had special powers or abilities?

I don't know about powers... but, yeah. I guess. 

Sometimes I just... I get to thinking I could fix the whole building myself. Like I should be the one teaching the bosses how to actually run the place. I just figure... maybe people all over town would end up knowing who I am. Because of my... my special way of seeing things. 

I don't really talk about it much, though. That's all.
During those times when you feel unusually high or energized, do you ever get so ill that you need to be hospitalized or can’t function at work or at home?

I don't know... I mean, I guess so. 

I've missed some shifts. Lost some cleaning jobs. People say... they say they can't understand me, or I'm not reliable. I don't go to the mosque much anymore, or see my family. They just... they don't get it. 

And... there was a time... I guess I got a little out of hand. Somebody called an ambulance. But I don't really want to talk about that.
During your depressed times, do you ever lose interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I guess so. I don't really do much of anything when I get like that. 

I used to... I liked taking pictures sometimes. Or playing chess. I'd go to the mosque, maybe cook a little something for the neighbors. But... I don't know. The camera just sits in the drawer now. And if people call, I just... I let it ring. I don't feel like answering.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a long-standing psychotic illness with both prominent mood episodes and clear periods of psychosis lasting at least 2 weeks in the absence of mood symptoms. There are also recurrent manic symptoms (decreased need for sleep, elevated/irritable mood, increased activity, grandiosity) and depressive episodes, but the key feature is that hallucinations and delusional beliefs persist outside mood episodes for weeks and over a course of years. This best fits schizoaffective disorder, manic type (ICD-10 F25.0) rather than bipolar disorder with psychotic features or schizophrenia alone.
